prompt:
Create ONE coherent mostly EXTERIOR ANTERIOR-THREE-QUARTER HEART WITH CONNECTED VASCULAR ROUTES, a nineteenth-century naturalistic engraved watercolor anatomical specimen on truly transparent background. Reference 1 supplies the exact wide paired OPEN pulmonary vascular trees, their original scale/canvas and fine branching appearance: retain their transparent spaces, with NO lung tissue, no opaque silhouettes and no alveolar blobs. Reference 2 is an ANATOMICAL GUIDE ONLY for exterior cardiac form, aorta/pulmonary-trunk depth, atrial auricles and superficial coronary grooves; ignore all its labels, leader lines, cartoon rendering and colors. Reference 3 supplies engraving/watercolor material style ONLY, not its ribs/lungs or full cutaway layout.

Place the normal adult heart centrally in the lower gap of the pulmonary trees, with naturally broad convex ANTERIOR ventricular walls. It is NOT a frontal four-chamber cross-section: keep at least 80% of its anterior epicardial surface physically intact, including the continuous anterior interventricular groove from base to apex. No exposed central septal cut face. Atria are externally bounded with natural auricles; left atrium and descending aorta are partly posterior/occluded. Two SMALL optional peripheral inspection windows may sit far laterally: a modest right-ventricular window toward viewer-left outer margin, a smaller thick-walled left-ventricular window at viewer-right outer margin. Neither reaches the central groove, exposes a broad septum or removes the anterior surface. If windows conflict with anatomy, omit them rather than opening the whole heart.

Blue pulmonary trunk emerges continuously from right ventricle on the anterior upper heart and branches into BOTH trees from reference 1. Red pulmonary veins return posteriorly into the left atrium with honest occlusion. One red ascending aorta emerges from left ventricle BEHIND the pulmonary trunk, arches upward with three natural major branches, then descends BEHIND the heart to a lower open cut end. There is one aortic root, no extra anterior valved cuff. Blue superior and inferior venae cavae enter the right atrium, with open specimen ends above and below.

On the actual convex OUTER EPICARDIAL WALL, show only a few readable representative coronary branches: a red anterior interventricular artery and companion blue vein run in the shallow EXTERIOR groove, with several tapered small branches onto intact muscle; right coronary course follows the retained basal/right-ventricular external groove. Coronary origins arise from aortic-root sides then pass naturally behind the pulmonary trunk/auricles—NO red bridge laid across the FRONT of the pulmonary trunk. Posterior venous drainage may remain hidden. Do not outline inspection windows with coronary vessels; do not put vessels on cut wall edges or exposed interior surfaces. Preserve clear depth, rounded heart volume and believable material attachments.

The entire result is one harmonious real anatomical preparation, not diagram symbols or collage. Same approximate1234x1275 canvas and scale as reference 1, heart broad around central lower x350–950,y500–1120. Fine sepia engraving, restrained coral muscle, ivory connective tissue, muted red arteries and slate-blue veins. Blank transparent background, no paper, text, labels, arrows, badges, detached enlargements, ribs, airways, lung parenchyma or extra specimens.
